newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Swedish CPI sparks hope of early rate cut.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swedish CPI sparks hope of early rate cut.

text.p: Analysts were expecting Sweden's central bank to cut interest rates as early as next week after the Consumer Price Index in January rose just 0.1 percent for a year-on-year fall of 0.1 percent.

Market expectation was for a CPI rise of 0.4 percent in January, an annualised rise of 0.2 percent, while the central bank, the Riksbank, forecast a year-on-year rise of between 0.5 and one percent in January.
This was the fourth consecutive month that Swedish year-on-year consumer prices ran at a negative annualised rate of inflation.
Analysts were in agreement that the figure signalled the Riksbank could make further cuts to its key repurchase rate, which currently stands at 4.10 percent.
"I think there is nothing hindering the Riksbank from cutting rates, maybe next week," said Jens Dalskov, the chief analysts at Den Danske Bank.
"Now it's just a question of time before the Riksbank cuts the repo again," said Peter Lindquist, HSBC Midland economist.
"This is a great figure for the market and particularly for the short interest rates."
The Riksbank cut the rate 25 times in 1996 from 8.91 percent but it has not cut the rate since December 17. The repo rate is its key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
Its other key rates, the deposit and lending rates, currently stand at 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent respectively.

Swedish bond yields opened lower on Thursday after the CPI figure, with the six month Treasury bill rate falling three basis points to 4.02 percent and the ten year bond yield sliding five basis points to 6.62 percent.
"All incoming information shows that there is room for repo cuts," said Bjorn Englund, economist at Unibank Markets.
"We stand by our forecast of a repo cut to 3.5 percent in the first half of 1997. We are expecting that domestic generated inflation is now under 1.5 percent."
Some analysts warned however, that crown stability was necessary before the Riksbank could further cut interest rates.
The Swedish currency has weakened significantly in recent weeks on uncertainty over fiscal policy and European economic and monetary union (EMU).
The Trade Currency Weighted (TCW) index, which measures the crown against a weighted basket of currencies, has risen beyond the Riksbank's recommended interval of 109 to 118 in real terms.
It is currently at 119.6 in nominal terms after peaking at 122.57 on February 6.
"This (CPI data) facilitates more repo rate cuts for the Riksbank even if they are steered by the crown in the short-term," said Nordbanken economist Tomas Pousette.
"(The CPI) was much lower than what we had expected. We had forecast a rise by 0.5 percent."
Statistics Sweden said lower interest rates cuts were a key element behind the CPI.
It said other costs for housing have increased and prices for clothing, shoes, transport, communication and food risen.

"The figure is much better than expected. Rent increases are lower than we had expected," said Knut Hallberg, a Swedbank economist. "This increases expectations that the Riksbank will lower the repo rate. It is more a question about when."
